claim: Amazon SNS follows the publish-subscribe messaging paradigm and delivers notifications to clients with a push mechanism, so clients do not need to poll for new information.
question: How does Amazon SNS deliver messages to subscribers?

values.display: publish-subscribe
eliminates the need to periodically check

evidence.quote: Amazon SNS follows the “publish-subscribe” (pub-sub) messaging paradigm, with notifications being delivered to clients using a “push” mechanism that eliminates the need to periodically check or “poll” for new information and updates.

claim: A topic is an access point that identifies a specific subject or event type, used to publish messages and to let clients subscribe for notifications.
question: What is an Amazon SNS topic?

values.display: identifying a specific subject or event type
allowing clients to subscribe for notifications

evidence.quote: Developers must first create a “topic” which is an “access point” – identifying a specific subject or event type – for publishing messages and allowing clients to subscribe for notifications.

claim: When a publisher publishes a message to a topic, Amazon SNS immediately delivers the message to all applicable subscribers.
question: What happens when a publisher publishes a message to an SNS topic?

values.display: publish a message to the topic
all applicable subscribers

evidence.quote: When publishers have information or updates to notify their subscribers about, they can publish a message to the topic – which immediately triggers Amazon SNS to deliver the message to all applicable subscribers.

claim: Amazon SQS lets distributed components of an application send and receive messages without requiring each component to be concurrently available.
question: How is Amazon SNS different from Amazon SQS?

values.display: without requiring each component to be concurrently available
send and receive messages

evidence.quote: Amazon SQS provides flexibility for distributed components of applications to send and receive messages without requiring each component to be concurrently available.

claim: A common pattern is to use SNS to publish messages to Amazon SQS queues to reliably send messages to one or many system components asynchronously.
question: What is a common pattern that combines Amazon SNS and Amazon SQS?

values.display: publish messages to Amazon SQS queues
one or many system components asynchronously

evidence.quote: A common pattern is to use SNS to publish messages to Amazon SQS queues to reliably send messages to one or many system components asynchronously.

claim: AWS recommends Amazon MQ when you move messaging of existing applications to the cloud quickly. Amazon MQ supports industry-standard APIs and protocols, so you can switch from a standards-based message broker without rewriting the messaging code.
question: How is Amazon SNS different from Amazon MQ?

values.display: existing applications
without rewriting the messaging code

evidence.quote: If you're using messaging with existing applications, and want to move your messaging to the cloud quickly and easily, we recommend you consider Amazon MQ. It supports industry-standard APIs and protocols so you can switch from any standards-based message broker to Amazon MQ without rewriting the messaging code in your applications.

claim: For brand new applications in the cloud AWS recommends Amazon SQS and Amazon SNS. You can use them to decouple and scale microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications, and improve reliability.
question: Which services does AWS recommend for new cloud applications instead of Amazon MQ?

values.display: brand new applications in the cloud
decouple and scale microservices

evidence.quote: If you are building brand new applications in the cloud, we recommend you consider Amazon SQS and Amazon SNS. Amazon SQS and SNS are lightweight, fully managed message queue and topic services that scale almost infinitely and provide simple, easy-to-use APIs. You can use Amazon SQS and SNS to decouple and scale microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications, and improve reliability.

claim: On a publish request, SNS stores multiple copies of the message to disk across multiple Availability Zones before it acknowledges receipt to the sender.
question: How durable is my data once published to Amazon SNS?

values.display: multiple copies (to disk)
multiple Availability Zones before acknowledging receipt

evidence.quote: Upon receiving a publish request, SNS stores multiple copies (to disk) of the message across multiple Availability Zones before acknowledging receipt of the request to the sender.

claim: Most of the time each message is delivered to your application exactly once, but the distributed nature of Amazon SNS and transient network conditions could result in occasional duplicate messages at the subscriber end. Applications should be designed so that processing a message more than once does not create errors or inconsistencies.
question: How many times will a subscriber receive each message?

values.display: occasional, duplicate messages
processing a message more than once

evidence.quote: Although most of the time each message will be delivered to your application exactly once, the distributed nature of Amazon SNS and transient network conditions could result in occasional, duplicate messages at the subscriber end. Developers should design their applications such that processing a message more than once does not create any errors or inconsistencies.

claim: Amazon SNS attempts to deliver messages in the order they were published into the topic, but network issues could result in out-of-order messages at the subscriber end.
question: Will messages be delivered to me in the exact order they were published?

values.display: attempt to deliver messages from the publisher in the order
out-of-order messages at the subscriber end

evidence.quote: The Amazon SNS service will attempt to deliver messages from the publisher in the order they were published into the topic. However, network issues could potentially result in out-of-order messages at the subscriber end.

claim: Once a message has been successfully published to a topic, it cannot be recalled.
question: Can a message be deleted after being published?

values.display: cannot be recalled
successfully published to a topic

evidence.quote: No, once a message has been successfully published to a topic, it cannot be recalled.

claim: All SNS notification messages contain a single published message.
question: Will a notification contain more than one message?

values.display: single published message
notification messages

evidence.quote: No, all notification messages will contain a single published message.

claim: Amazon SNS delivers a message to the subscribed endpoint as long as the endpoint is accessible. A delivery fails when SNS cannot access the endpoint because of a client-side or a server-side error.
question: Does Amazon SNS guarantee that messages are delivered to the subscribed endpoint?

values.display: as long as the subscribed endpoint is accessible
client-side or a server-side error

evidence.quote: Yes, as long as the subscribed endpoint is accessible. A message delivery fails when Amazon SNS can't access a subscribed endpoint, due to either a client-side or a server-side error.

claim: After a client-side error, or a server-side error that continues beyond the retries set by the retry policy, Amazon SNS discards the message unless a dead-letter queue is attached to the subscription.
question: What does SNS do with a message it cannot deliver after all retries?

values.display: discards the message
unless a dead-letter queue is attached to the subscription

evidence.quote: When Amazon SNS receives a client-side error, or continues to receive a server-side error for a message beyond the number of retries specified by the corresponding retry policy, Amazon SNS discards the message — unless a dead-letter queue is attached to the subscription.

claim: If a message cannot be delivered on the first attempt, Amazon SNS runs a 4-phase retry policy: retries with no delay, retries with minimum delay, retries according to a back-off model, and retries with maximum delay.
question: What happens to Amazon SNS messages if the subscribing endpoint is not available?

values.display: 4-phase retry policy
retries according to a back-off model

evidence.quote: If a message cannot be successfully delivered on the first attempt, Amazon SNS executes a 4-phase retry policy: 1) retries with no delay in between attempts, 2) retries with minimum delay between attempts, 3) retries according to a back-off model, and 4) retries with maximum delay between attempts.

claim: When the message delivery retry policy is exhausted, Amazon SNS can move the message to a dead-letter queue (DLQ).
question: Where can SNS move a message when its delivery retry policy is exhausted?

values.display: move the message to a dead-letter queue
retry policy is exhausted

evidence.quote: When the message delivery retry policy is exhausted, Amazon SNS can move the message to a dead-letter queue (DLQ).

claim: With message filtering, Amazon SNS topic subscribers can selectively receive only a subset of the messages they are interested in, instead of all messages published to the topic.
question: Can subscribers selectively receive only a subset of messages published to a topic?

values.display: selectively receive only a subset
as opposed to receiving all messages published to a topic

evidence.quote: Message filtering enables Amazon SNS topic subscribers to selectively receive only a subset of the messages they are interested in, as opposed to receiving all messages published to a topic.

claim: To fan out identical messages to multiple SQS queues, create an SNS topic and subscribe multiple SQS standard queues to it. Whenever a message is sent to the topic, SNS delivers it to all the subscribed queues.
question: How can I fanout identical messages to multiple SQS queues?

values.display: subscribe multiple SQS standard queues to the SNS topic
fanned out to the SQS queues

evidence.quote: Create an SNS topic first using SNS. Then create and subscribe multiple SQS standard queues to the SNS topic. Now whenever a message is sent to the SNS topic, the message will be fanned out to the SQS queues, i.e. SNS will deliver the message to all the SQS queues that are subscribed to the topic.

claim: A topic can support subscriptions and notification deliveries over multiple transports.
question: Can a single topic support subscriptions over multiple protocols or transports?

values.display: multiple transports
subscriptions and notification deliveries

evidence.quote: A topic can support subscriptions and notification deliveries over multiple transports.

claim: When delivery to subscribers must be in order (first-in-first-out) and once only, and you want SNS to handle it, SNS FIFO topics are the way to go.
question: What are SNS FIFO topics?

values.display: in order (first-in-first-out), and once only
SNS FIFO topics is the way to go

evidence.quote: When the delivery of those messages to subscribers must be in order (first-in-first-out), and once only, and you want SNS to take care of it, SNS FIFO topics is the way to go.

claim: Amazon SNS FIFO topics can deliver ordered messages to Amazon SQS FIFO queues to provide consistent end-to-end message ordering for distributed applications.
question: Can SNS FIFO topics deliver ordered messages to Amazon SQS?

values.display: deliver ordered messages to Amazon Simple Queue Service
consistent end-to-end message ordering

evidence.quote: Amazon SNS FIFO topics can deliver ordered messages to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues to provide consistent end-to-end message ordering for distributed applications.

claim: When strict ordering is not necessary, Amazon SNS FIFO topics can also deliver messages to Amazon SQS standard queues.
question: Can an SNS FIFO topic deliver to an SQS standard queue?

values.display: deliver messages to Amazon SQS standard queues
strict ordering is not necessary

evidence.quote: When strict ordering is not necessary, Amazon FIFO topics can also deliver messages to Amazon SQS standard queues, offering flexibility in how you design your applications.
